requirements.name: collapsible thread tools drawer
key UX: The composer shows a left-side toggle button that opens and closes a bottom drawer for thread-level actions.
The drawer surfaces New Thread, Rollback, and Compact close to the typing area so thread maintenance does not require leaving the chat surface.
The toggle button reflects drawer state with an active style and chevron direction change.

requirements.name: context-aware action availability
key UX: New Thread is disabled while restarting, when no workspace is open, or when workspace switching is currently blocked.
Rollback and Compact are disabled when there is no active thread or when actions are blocked by runtime state.
The send button and input availability follow workspace presence, waiting-for-input state, restart state, and interrupt-pending state.

requirements.name: keyboard-first message composition
key UX: Pressing Enter submits the draft for a normal chat send.
Pressing Shift+Enter keeps multiline authoring available inside the textarea.
The composer keeps a standard form submit path so both keyboard submit and button submit converge on the same send behavior.

requirements.name: draft lifecycle that respects submit results
key UX: The draft is stored locally in the shell and updates on every input change.
A successful send clears the draft so the next turn starts from a clean input.
A failed or rejected send keeps the existing draft in place so the user does not lose what they typed.

requirements.name: turn-state aware send and stop control
key UX: The primary composer action shows Send while idle and switches to Stop while a turn is in progress.
Submitting the form during an active turn triggers interrupt instead of starting a second send.
The stop icon can show a spinning pending state while interruption is being processed.

requirements.name: adaptive multiline textarea growth
key UX: The textarea auto-resizes to content by measuring scroll height after draft changes.
The field grows when the draft wraps or contains explicit line breaks, and shrinks again when content becomes shorter.
The auto-growth is capped by a fixed composer max height so the input does not consume the whole mobile viewport.

requirements.name: textarea overflow only after max-height is reached
key UX: The composer textarea now keeps growing naturally until it reaches its configured max height.
A vertical scrollbar appears only after the measured content height exceeds the max-height cap.
When content is below the cap, the textarea keeps its scrollbar hidden so the field feels like one expanding input surface.

requirements.name: comfortable default composer height around 2.5 lines
key UX: The default empty-state typing box now starts at a 64px min height so it feels more like a short multiline surface than a single-line field.
The taller default keeps the mobile layout compact while making short prompts and edits more comfortable to author.
The composer still uses the same auto-grow and max-height behavior after the new default height is applied.

requirements.name: stateful placeholders and disabled feedback
key UX: The textarea placeholder changes from 'Send to Codex' to 'Waiting…' when input is unavailable.
Disabled state reduces opacity and blocks editing to match runtime lock conditions.
The composer remains visible even when input is unavailable so users understand where chat resumes.

requirements.name: composer-adjacent todo list panel
key UX: When an active todo list exists, a standalone panel appears above the composer and summarizes total and completed tasks.
The panel can be collapsed and re-expanded without losing the current plan context.
The panel updates when todo content changes and re-expands when thread or workspace context changes, keeping the visible plan aligned with the current conversation.
